issues.failure_explanation: Smooth convexity alone does not provide a uniform stochastic O(1/k) guarantee. For example, noisy quadratic oracles with curvature proportional to k^{-1/2} and minimizers at two fixed, separated points cannot reliably distinguish those minimizers from k bounded-variance observations, leaving worst-case error of order k^{-1/2}. The paper's actual O(1/k) baseline requires a positive strong-convexity constant and corresponding stepsize conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: A gradient Lipschitz bound controls the absolute values of Hessian eigenvalues, not merely their upper endpoints. With M=I and F(x)=-a x^2/2 for a>L, the sole Hessian eigenvalue is -a≤L, but the gradient's Lipschitz constant is a>L. The lemma does not assume convexity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the one-sided condition by eigenvalues lying in [-L,L], or explicitly assume convexity in the one-sided characterization, and make the same correction in its repetitions.
issues.overall_effect: The stated general spectral equivalence and its repetitions are false for indefinite or negative curvature. The strongly convex applications do not require the false extension.
issues.title: The Hessian characterization of gradient Lipschitz continuity is one-sided
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local spectral correction; the convergence results already assuming strong convexity retain their substantive guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: The event Ω∞ depends on future samples and is not F_k-measurable. An inequality for E[X|F_k] therefore cannot be converted into the same inequality for E[X|F_k,Ω∞]. Survival conditioning changes the gradient distribution, and the stated moment assumptions do not hold automatically under that changed law. Positive probability of Ω∞ is also not assured.

issues.failure_explanation: Convex outer losses give a GGN matrix of the form ∑J_nᵀ A_n J_n with A_n positive semidefinite. This need not be positive definite: any common Jacobian null direction remains null. The analogous automatic Fisher definiteness claim also needs an identifiability/nondegeneracy condition. For a regular Gaussian model with mean θ_1+θ_2, both matrices are proportional to the singular all-ones 2×2 matrix.

failure_location.quote: This generalized Gauss-Newton matrix (GGN), which ignores second order information of $b_n$, is SPD when $a_n$ is convex even when the true Hessian is indefinite.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State positive semidefiniteness, identify sufficient full-rank/identifiability conditions for strict definiteness, and require positive regularization when those conditions fail.
issues.overall_effect: The automatic invertibility and admissibility of these undamped curvature matrices as SPD metrics are not established, particularly in the flat and overparameterized setting emphasized by the paper.
issues.title: Positive semidefiniteness is incorrectly promoted to strict definiteness
issues.why_classification: The automatic SPD promise must be replaced by additional nondegeneracy conditions or a regularized construction, while comparable curvature-aware methods remain available.

issues.failure_explanation: Exponential-family membership alone does not identify the GGN for an arbitrary loss decomposition with the Fisher matrix. For Bernoulli probability p=sigmoid(θ), take b(θ)=p and the outer loss to be cross-entropy. With observed label y=1, the GGN is (1-p)², while the model Fisher is p(1-p). They differ unless p=1/2. Using the natural parameter as the model output, or an appropriate model expectation, is an additional condition.

failure_location.quote: For models trained with exponential-family losses, the FIM coincides with the GGN~\citep{martens_new_2020, schraudolph_fast_2002}.
